label: changing-land
prompt: Use case: illustration-story. Asset type: THREE separate tall portrait game backgrounds arranged as equal-width columns side by side, without gutters, frames or dividing rules. Each portrait is approximately 1:2.16, overall canvas approximately 3:2.16. Create full rectangular paintings, NOT icons. The supplied images are style/continuity references: luminous opaque gouache, selective fine ink, lapis, jade, burnt ochre, muted coral, warm ivory light. Monumental and intimate, a world being created, never a settlement. No text, numbers, words, ornamental borders, people unless explicitly specified, buildings, UI or watermark. Place dramatic landmarks mainly in the UPPER 42 percent of EACH portrait; the LOWER 58 percent must be a spacious calm medium-LIGHT desaturated blue-grey/ochre painted foreground with sparse broad atmospheric strokes, giving dark circular tokens readable working space. This calm area belongs naturally to each painting, not a rectangular UI panel or flat overlay. Preserve the three equal portrait panels. Recurring geography when visible: hooked ochre headland at upper left, a single arched cave at its foot when the requested era permits a cave, teal tidal inlet, pale dry rock shelf on the RIGHT inside the entrance and a broad dry upper interior wall above the tidal wash. The dry shelf is connected to exposed rock at the mouth, visibly above the water; do not flood the whole floor. Distant jagged coastal hills, pale Moon with a pair of adjacent unequal craters, consistent with reference. No actual Earth map. LEFT: Same hooked cave coast now mantled with a flowering forest. Broadleaf trees, restrained coral and ivory blossoms and a few tiny winged pollinators in the upper landscape, still immense sky and sea. No people, no icy peaks, no grazing mammal herd. Quiet pale water/ochre foreground below. CENTER: An immense high overview across the SAME coastal world: the hooked cave headland is a small anchor at left, a mountain range separates jade wet forest from a dry ochre rain-shadow basin at right, a small glacier sits only on the distant high peaks, and a braided river crosses a gravel valley. Two tiny long-necked browsers may appear on the forest ridge. NO green oasis or pond in the dry basin, no human figures or buildings, no advanced ice sheet. Keep composition broad and legible, lower field spacious pale river/sand atmosphere. RIGHT: Same hooked cave coast after the impact winter, beginning to recover. Broken dark fern-tree trunks remain on the upper ridge, but a few small bright GREEN SHOOTS emerge from sheltered earth. Light has returned. NO living giant browsers, no standing mature forest, no human figures, no mammal herd. The loss remains visible; new life is tentative. Dry cave wall remains and lower space stays calm pale blue-grey.
